chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who have faith.
But [He granted authority] over those who take him as their guardian and disobey His command.

key_terms.يَتَوَلَّوْنَهُمْ: Those who take him as guardian/ally

ai.seo_question: Who does Satan have authority over according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq’s clarification that Satan’s *sultan* (authority) is not inherent or absolute but contingent upon human choice, specifically their voluntary submission through *khalw* (obedience) or *shiqq* (disobedience) to God. This distinction underscores the Shia theological principle of free will, affirming that the righteous are never fully enslaved by Satan unless they choose to follow his whispers, thereby preserving the justice of divine recompense.
